body.text: Not all stress is bad. Some stress helps. At times it gives the push before a deadline, or an exam, can sharpen you up. The problem is stress that persists long after (or during) whatever caused it has the ability to wear on you both mentally (constantly on edge) and physically (poor sleep, appetite changes, stomach issues). It is your fight-or-flight response got stuck in overdrive.

body.text: Well done. Tomorrow, we look at the link between stress and your thoughts.
Your thoughts, feeling and emotions have a direct connection with your sleep. Negative thoughts heighten alertness and delay sleep. Calmer thoughts do the opposite.

Some of our stress is self-created: our thoughts build scenarios that aren't always accurate, and it costs us anyway. Procrastination often comes from an exaggerated fear of a task, not the task itself. Challenging these patterns takes a bit of effort, but it's a learnable skill.

blocks.title: Six Questions to Challenge a Thought

notes.text: When faced with a situation where your thought feels bigger than a situation, ask yourself these questions.
Am I overreacting? Will this matter in a few months?
Am I going on opinion or isolated experience, not facts?
Am I assuming I know how someone else feels or will react?
Am I seeing this in black and white, with nothing in between?
Is there real evidence this thought isn't entirely true?
What would I tell a friend who had this exact thought?
Come back to this whenever a thought feels bigger than the situation.
P.S. Once a user has read this card, they should be able to pull this up anytime they like to refer to it.

body.text: Pick one thought from your log and run it through these questions. Notice what shifted.
